desktop_mission.mission_sub: Pascal's Hydrostatic Law, Force Amplification & Work Invariance
desktop_mission.voice_mission: Today we're simulating the hydraulic press and Pascal's principle in Kotlin.
math_cards: Pressure applied to an enclosed static fluid transmits undiminished to every point in the vessel
Widening output ram diameter scales output crushing force quadratically with mechanical advantage
Fluid incompressibility preserves energy: output force multiplies while output stroke shrinks proportionally
desktop_mission.voice_math: The core physics: Pascal's pressure transmission, quadratic force multiplication, and work conservation.

math_steps.badge: EQUATION 1 OF 3 • PASCAL'S ENCLOSED PRESSURE LAW
math_steps.note: Effort applied to the narrow input piston pressurizes the entire hydraulic fluid reservoir uniformly
math_steps.sub_desc: Evaluates fluid pressure generated by input plunger effort.

math_steps.note: The output ram integrates fluid pressure across a vastly larger area, amplifying crushing force up to 100x
math_steps.code:
// 2. Mechanical advantage and output crushing force
val mechanicalAdvantage = a2M2 / max(a1M2, 1e-7f)
val outputForceN = inputForceN * mechanicalAdvantage
val outputForceKg = outputForceN / 9.81f
math_steps.sub_desc: Multiplies input effort by the cross-sectional area ratio.

math_steps.note: Energy is strictly conserved: high output force requires a proportionately smaller ram travel distance
math_steps.code:
// 3. Incompressible volume conservation and work invariance
val currentD1M = maxStrokeD1M * inputStrokeFrac
val currentD2M = currentD1M * (a1M2 / a2M2)
val workJoules = inputForceN * currentD1M
math_steps.sub_desc: Calculates ram stroke reduction and conserved mechanical work.

mystery.en: How can a light hand push crush solid steel blocks under thousands of pounds of hydraulic force?

en.title: Hydraulic Press
en.teaser: Enclosed fluids transmit pressure equally in all directions, turning small plunger inputs into massive crushing loads.

en.hook: How can a human hand pushing with just ten pounds of force crush solid steel under thousands of pounds of power?
en.math: Pascal's principle transmits fluid pressure equally everywhere, scaling output force quadratically with piston diameter.
en.question: Can we simulate a hydraulic press, crushing deformation, and work invariance live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We integrate Pascal's pressure equations, model plastic crushing strains, and render hydraulic manifolds on Canvas.
en.payoff: The hydraulic press and Pascal force multiplier running live in Kotlin.
